minors.description: Ramayyan's off-panel line 'They questioned you.' has its tail pointing up to the top edge, right beside Varma's extended arm, so it reads as the king speaking. Nagoji's hands are clasped together in front of him, not 'still at his sides'.
minors.evidence: The tail tip of 'They questioned you.' sits at the top border directly above Varma's wrist and bangle. Nagoji's two bandaged hands overlap at the centre of his body.

minors.description: The gate guards are bare-chested with brown leather cross-straps. The script asks for white cotton with dark sashes, and no matchlocks are visible (spears only). Behind the gate stands a whitewashed two-storey building with a red-tiled roof and a tower, which reads as a Portuguese colonial villa. It does not match the hall on carved pillars established in 1.3.
minors.evidence: Guards at the left and right of the frame wear only straps and dhotis. The white villa sits centre background, behind Ibrahim's turban.

minors.description: The beat 'one bandaged hand shaping a low wall in the air' is missing. Nagoji is cropped at the shoulders and no hand shows.
minors.evidence: Only Nagoji's head and upper shirt are in frame, with the bastion stain behind him.

minors.description: The script makes Ibrahim's LEFT-jaw scar catch the sea light in this panel, which is the stated reason for the hall plan. He is drawn small and frontal with the sea behind him, and no scar is legible.
minors.evidence: Ibrahim is a full figure, face about 60 px tall at full resolution, with no visible scar line on either jaw.

minors.description: The script names this frame as the future reference image for Ramayyan, but the panel's top edge crops his head at the brow. His 'receding hair' does not show, and he reads younger and fuller-haired than the balding Ramayyan of 2.2 and later pages.
minors.evidence: The panel border cuts through his hairline. In 2.2, 3.3, 5.3 and later he has a bald crown with curly sides.

minors.description: The script's lettering convention calls for the '[in Malayalam]' tag to be set in italic in a small balloon. Every instance in the chapter is set upright.
minors.evidence: '[in Malayalam]' balloons on 3.3, 4.5, 5.3, 6.1, 6.4, 7.3, 9.2, 9.4 and 10.2 all use upright lettering.

minors.description: The script asks for the closing forge-and-blade line as a 'separate, weighted' caption. It is lettered in the same plain caption box as every other caption, so the chapter's last line gets no extra weight.
minors.evidence: The top-right caption 'For now, Travancore was the forge...' uses the standard white box and font.
